summary: NextHarvest is a geospatial decision-support mobile app that transforms NASA Earth observation data (POWER, SMAP, OpenET, MODIS/Landsat, SRTM) and soil/yield databases (USDA SSURGO, NASS, FAO GAEZ) into ranked, explainable 3-to-5-year crop rotation plans. Farmers draw or select their field, simulate climate shifts (rainfall, temperature, irrigation), and compare at least three multi-season rotation options with transparent scores for soil health, water efficiency, and climate risk.
details:
What exactly does it do and how does it work? NextHarvest is an agroclimatic decision-support mobile application and geospatial API that transforms NASA Earth observation datasets and USDA soil and yield databases into transparent, explainable crop rotation plans. Instead of overwhelming farmers with raw NetCDF/HDF5 satellite files or giving opaque AI prescriptions, our platform guides producers and agronomists through a 5-step field adaptation workflow:

  1. Field Mapping: The farmer draws their field polygon boundary directly on the interactive satellite map in the Flutter app (e.g., an alfalfa parcel in Churchill County, Nevada) or submits GeoJSON coordinates to our FastAPI backend.
  2. Multi-Sensor Data Fusion: The backend queries NASA POWER (agroclimatology at the centroid), OpenET (field-scale evapotranspiration demand), and USDA NRCS SSURGO (soil profile across the polygon) in parallel, harmonizing them into a single field diagnostic.
  3. Field Health & Vulnerability Verdict: A deterministic engine evaluates water balance deficits, calculates root-zone moisture Z-score anomalies (smap_rootzone_anomaly_z via NASA POWER GWETROOT), identifies bare-soil erosion windows (bare_field_months), and assigns clear health status badges.
  4. Priority Customization & TOPSIS Ranking: The farmer sets 6 priority sliders (Water savings, Soil organic matter, Erosion control, Pest cycle break, Forage value, and Market income) along with irrigation and machinery constraints. Our Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (TOPSIS) engine and USDA NASS county yield lookup rank three distinct rotation strategies—including the current crop baseline—with a 6-axis comparison radar and a 5-section evidence breakdown (Why suggested, Supporting evidence, Expected benefits, Information gaps, and Risks requiring local review).
  5. Real-Time Climate Scenario Stress-Testing: Using interactive climate sliders, the farmer adjusts annual rainfall (-30% to +30%) and temperature warming (+0 °C to +4 °C) to immediately recalculate how each rotation holds up under drought or heatwaves without triggering new external NASA calls.

What benefits does it offer? NextHarvest removes three major barriers facing small and mid-sized producers: fragmented satellite data formats, complex water-soil-crop trade-offs, and unverified black-box recommendations. In under 30 seconds, farmers can compare side-by-side multi-year rotation options (such as transitioning from water-intensive continuous alfalfa to a drought-resilient Sorghum -> Winter Triticale Cover -> Chickpea sequence) and see exactly how much irrigation water is saved, how winter cover crops protect bare soil from erosion, and how legume/grass alternations break pest and pathogen cycles.

What is the intended impact of the project? Our intended impact aligns directly with the UN Sustainable Development Goals, specifically SDG 2 (Zero Hunger & Sustainable Agriculture), SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sustainable Withdrawals), SDG 13 (Climate Action), and SDG 15 (Life on Land / Soil Restoration). Grounded in real-world challenges like water-scarce alfalfa farming in Churchill County, Nevada, NextHarvest helps farmers reduce synthetic nitrogen and water consumption, helps agricultural cooperatives audit climate resilience across multiple parcels, and preserves long-term soil organic matter.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use? We built a modular, full-stack geospatial architecture designed for reliability and low-bandwidth rural environments:

  • Mobile & Web Frontend: Built with Dart and Flutter using Riverpod for reactive state management, Dio for resilient networking, and interactive map polygon drawing for field boundary capture.
  • Geospatial & Decision Backend: Developed in Python 3.12+ with FastAPI, Pydantic v2, and async HTTPX clients, backed by PostgreSQL + PostGIS (GeoAlchemy2 / Shapely) for spatial WKT polygon persistence and Redis caching.
  • Earth Observation & Agronomic APIs: Integrates NASA POWER (precipitation, temperature, EVPTRNS, GWETROOT), OpenET (polygon evapotranspiration), USDA NRCS Soil Data Access (SSURGO), US FCC Census Area API (county FIPS resolution), and USDA NASS QuickStats (historical county crop yields).
  • Hybrid Statistical + Grounded SI Layer: Combines non-parametric trend estimation (Theil-Sen slope), Z-score anomaly detection, and TOPSIS multi-criteria ranking with an optional multi-provider LLM explainer (OpenAI / Google Gemini structured outputs via ai_explainer.py) and an automated pytest suite.

What is the creative aspect of your project? Our biggest creative differentiator is combining Interactive Climate Stress-Testing Sliders with Bare-Soil Vulnerability Window Detection and 5-Dimension Scientific Governance. Instead of giving a single static crop prescription, NextHarvest treats the farm as a living laboratory: it detects the exact months a parcel is left bare and exposed to runoff, inserts targeted cover crops into those windows, and lets the farmer stress-test their rotation against a -25% rainfall drop or +2 °C heatwave in real time. Furthermore, our built-in science glossary (GET /api/v1/glossary/explain) educates users on the difference between satellite model proxies (9–50 km scale) and in-situ soil probes.

What factors did your team consider? Our team prioritized Agronomic Safety, Zero AI Hallucinations, and Transparent Governance. Because an incorrect crop recommendation can ruin a harvest, we enforced a strict architectural boundary: Super Intelligence (LLMs) is never allowed to invent numbers, select crops, or alter mathematical scores. All water balances, soil health metrics, and rotation rankings are computed 100% deterministically by our Python agronomic engine; SI is used only to rewrite the structured explanation sections into clear language, with a deterministic English template fallback if the AI service is offline.In accordance with NASA Space Apps rules, we also disclose that SI tools (Google Antigravity / Gemini and OpenAI-compatible models) assisted with coding, testing, documentation translation, and our 30-second demo voiceover, without using or modifying any NASA logos or branding.

Next Steps & Future Roadmap: To scale NextHarvest from our validated MVP to global precision agriculture, our next steps include: (1) upgrading root-zone moisture from our NASA POWER GWETROOT proxy to direct 9 km NASA SMAP L4 and 70 m ECOSTRESS feeds via AppEEARS; (2) integrating 10-meter optical bare-soil detection via Sentinel-2 (Copernicus CDSE) and Harmonized Landsat-Sentinel (HLS); (3) subdividing fields into 30-meter H3 hexagonal grids for intra-field variable-rate rotations; (4) adding live USDA AMS market prices and EMBRAPA ZARC soil/climate rules for South America; and (5) enabling full offline model execution on the mobile device.
